key_business_initiatives.title: AI across products and operations
key_business_initiatives.text: The company has integrated AI into its products and technology. It also uses AI to improve developer productivity and the speed of resolution in customer service teams. In the second quarter 2026 release, the Chief Executive Officer described using AI to innovate faster and operate more efficiently. Management believes products improved by machine learning and AI will continue to drive greater retention, repeat and direct business.

key_business_initiatives.title: Unified technology platform
key_business_initiatives.text: In 2023, the company moved the Hotels.com and Vrbo front-end stacks onto the Brand Expedia stack. Its platform focus is on configurable technical capabilities that support various travel products on standard architecture. Management believes this strategy will enable it to ship new capabilities and features faster. All transaction-based businesses now run on the shared platform infrastructure.

key_business_initiatives.title: B2B segment growth
key_business_initiatives.text: The company intends to grow B2B by increasing wallet share with existing customers and winning new customer contracts. It also plans to grow B2B by introducing additional products and services. Management expects to continue to cement its B2B leadership as B2B benefits from B2C product and technology work. B2B partners can connect through the Rapid API or adopt customized white label or co-branded templates.

key_business_initiatives.title: Global lodging supply expansion
key_business_initiatives.text: The company continues to expand the breadth and depth of its global hotel offering. Specific initiatives are intended to drive greater global size and scale through faster room night growth. In some cases, the company has reduced its economics in various geographies based on local market conditions. In the second quarter 2026 release, the Chief Executive Officer said the company expanded supply across its business.

Ongoing initiatives target transactional efficiencies, particularly in payments and customer service.
